articles.title: Asian shares mostly decline after AI stocks lead a rebound on Wall Street
articles.description: Asian shares are mostly lower after stocks artificial-intelligence-related stocks bounced back on Wall Street while other sectors continued to be shaky and oil prices stayed high. Benchmarks fell in early Tuesday trading in Japan, Australia and South Korea. Shares also fell in Hong Kong but were little changed in Shanghai. The S&P 500 rose 0.4%, coming off its worst week since June, and the Nasdaq composite rallied 1.1%. The majority of U.S. stocks outside of AI and tech fell, though, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average finished with a 0.1% drop. Nvidia added 1.4%, one of the strongest forces lifting the S&P 500.

articles.title: US stocks rise after oil prices retreat and companies deliver strong profits
articles.description: The U.S. stock market is rising following reports showing strong profits for Equifax, Hasbro and other companies, while oil prices eased back after nearing their highest levels since the war with Iran began. The S&P 500 climbed 0.6% Tuesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 667 points, while more swings for the artificial-intelligence industry had the Nasdaq composite up a more modest 0.5%. After nearing $112 in the morning, the price for a barrel of Brent crude oil fell back below $107. That helped the broad U.S. stock market erase early-morning losses. So did a swing for several AI stocks from drops to gains.

articles.title: US futures dip as AI sell-off returns and oil prices rise sharply
articles.description: U.S. futures are mostly lower as artificial-intelligence-related stocks are under pressure again and oil prices rise while fighting continues in the Middle East. Futures for the S&P 500 fell 0.1% on Tuesday, while those for the Nasdaq declined 0.5%. Futures for the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.2%. Shares of South Korea’s AI company Elice Group tumbled 30% in their first day of trading as investors remain wary following a recent tech selloff. Elice’s slump pulled down others in the sector, including CoreWeave, whose stock slipped 4.5% before the market open.
